references.text: The psalm describes the Lord as the shepherd who leads the people, an image that Jesus makes concrete by saying that whoever enters through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
The Lord is described as a shepherd who gathers the lambs and leads them, which reflects Jesus' claim that whoever enters through the gate is the legitimate shepherd of the sheep.

Jesus expands on this image immediately after verse 2 by saying that he himself is the gate, and that whoever enters through it will be saved, directly linking the gate to his identity as the shepherd.
Jesus confirms that he is the good shepherd who knows his sheep, an identity he establishes in verse 2 by defining whoever enters through the gate as the shepherd.
